name: Motor Scooter
description: A low-speed motorcycle with a step-through frame or a footrest platform, wheels over 16 inches, 2 or more brake horsepower (1,500 W) and a design speed of no more than 50 mph. Its definition is written in engine terms (over 50 cc), but Kentucky counts a plug-in battery-powered one as an electric motorcycle.

restrictions.rule: A step-through frame or a platform for the operator's feet, and wheels more than 16 inches in diameter
2 brake horsepower (1,500 W) or more, designed to go no faster than 50 mph
Not a moped: Kentucky's moped definition requires a combustion engine of 50 cc or less
Riders need a motorcycle operator's license or motorcycle instruction permit
Under the motorcycle helmet law: riders and passengers under 21, permit holders and riders licensed less than a year must wear a helmet
Titled and registered as a motorcycle; a plug-in battery-powered one also pays Kentucky's annual electric motorcycle fee
Must be insured, with proof of insurance carried while riding
Must meet the same equipment standards as a motorcycle and follow the rules of the road
